title: auth.org.created payload
description:
Payload for `auth.org.created`, published by Auth when provisioning creates an organisation (FR-15.4, ADR-0022). Auth is the source of truth for the organisation record; this event is how every other service learns of one without polling.

Published only when the organisation is **created** — the provisioning path is idempotent on `registration_id`, and a replayed registration finds the existing organisation and emits nothing. That is the acceptance criterion in FR-15, and it is the difference between an onboarding loop and an onboarding storm.

The envelope's `org_id` is this organisation, not the actor's. Provisioning runs in a console command or an event handler, where there is no authenticated user to take a tenant from, so it publishes inside `TenantContext::runFor()`.

The file name is the routing key — `SchemaDiscovery` keys the catalog by it, so renaming this file silently removes the contract.

org_id.description: The new organisation's id, matching the `org_id` claim (ADR-0001) and the envelope's own `org_id`.

status.description: Present even though a newly created organisation is always `active`: a consumer projecting this row should store what it was told rather than a constant, or the first `auth.org.updated` will find a column it has never written.

registration_id.description: `source_registration_id` — the registration this organisation was provisioned from (ADR-0022). Null when it was created by other means. A consumer may use it for idempotency alongside `abeon_processed_events`; the two guard different things, one against redelivery of a message and one against a second registration for the same onboarding.

owner_user_id.description: The owner's platform-wide user id, as a string. The owner is a membership holding the owner role, not a flag on the user — this is here so a consumer need not ask Auth a second question to know who to address.
